title: Multiplicative-type groups split on an etale covering
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $H$ a group object in schemes over $U$, with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Suppose there is an fppf covering $\{V_\alpha\to U\}$ [def-pc-fppf-site], finitely generated additive abelian groups $M_\alpha$, and isomorphisms of $V_\alpha$-group schemes $H\times_UV_\alpha\simeq D_{V_\alpha}(M_\alpha)$ [def-pc-base-change]. Here $D_W(M)$ is obtained by gluing $D_A(M)=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ on affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset W$, with the Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Then there is a jointly surjective family of etale morphisms $U_j\to U$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], with each $U_j$ affine, finitely generated additive abelian groups $N_j$, and isomorphisms of $U_j$-group schemes $H\times_UU_j\simeq D_{U_j}(N_j)$. No Noetherian, reducedness, smoothness, connectedness or torsion-order restriction is imposed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition B.3.4, printed pp.291–292: étale-local splitting of fppf forms of diagonalizable groups of finite type. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this group-scheme theorem.

proof.text: For a finitely generated abelian group $M$, write $P_M=D_U(M)$. Its formation commutes with arbitrary base change: on affine charts the maps $B\otimes_A A[M]\rightleftarrows B[M]$, $b\otimes ae_m\mapsto ba e_m$ and $be_m\mapsto b\otimes e_m$, are inverse algebra maps and respect the three Hopf operations on every basis element. The affine fibre-product formula and affine adjunction give the corresponding group-scheme isomorphisms. Their formulas agree on restrictions, so scheme-morphism gluing gives the assertion for arbitrary test schemes. Fix the given fppf covering $\{V_\alpha\to U\}$ and splittings $P_{M_\alpha}|_{V_\alpha}\simeq H|_{V_\alpha}$. All families below are sets in the size convention.

For each covering index $\beta$, define $F_\beta(Z)=\operatorname{Isom}_{Z\text{-gp}}(P_{M_\beta}|_Z,H|_Z)$ on $U$-schemes. This is an fppf sheaf. Indeed, for a compatible family of group isomorphisms on a covering $\{Z_a\to Z\}$, its base changes to $P_{M_\beta}|_Z$ and $H|_Z$ are fppf coverings and hence fpqc coverings. Representable descent glues the maps and their inverses uniquely. Applying its uniqueness clause after base change to the relevant products proves that the two composites are identities and that the glued maps preserve multiplication, identity and inverse. Thus the glued map belongs to $F_\beta(Z)$, uniquely.

Put $E_{\beta\alpha}=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathbf Z}(M_\alpha,M_\beta)$ and $L_{\beta\alpha}=\coprod_{e\in E_{\beta\alpha}}V_\alpha$. The chosen splitting identifies $F_\beta|_{V_\alpha}$ with $h_{L_{\beta\alpha}}$. To check this on any $V_\alpha$-scheme $Z$, cover $Z$ by affine opens. Character duality on each nonempty affine says that a homomorphism between these split diagonalizable groups is uniquely locally $D(u)$, for $u:M_\alpha\to M_\beta$. Applying the same assertion to an inverse shows that isomorphisms correspond precisely to locally constant maps to $E_{\beta\alpha}$. The labels agree on overlaps by uniqueness. Conversely such labels define $D(u)$ and $D(u^{-1})$ on their open-and-closed fibres; scheme gluing gives inverse group morphisms on $Z$. The coproduct statement identifies morphisms $Z\to L_{\beta\alpha}$ with exactly these labelled open-and-closed decompositions. The correspondence commutes with restriction. Empty opens contribute no condition, and an empty label set gives the empty scheme.

source.place: Appendix B.1, printed pp.280-281, character description; explicit agent deduction of the split-isomorphism functor.

proof.text: Form $A_\beta=\coprod_\alpha L_{\beta\alpha}$ with the map $q_\beta:h_{A_\beta}\to F_\beta$ given by step 3. For a $U$-scheme $Z$ and $a\in F_\beta(Z)$, the sheaf $h_Z\times_{F_\beta}h_{A_\beta}$ is represented by $\coprod_\alpha(Z\times_UV_\alpha)$. In fact, on the $\alpha$ component, once a map to $Z\times_UV_\alpha$ is specified, the required lift into $L_{\beta\alpha}$ is the unique point corresponding to the restriction of $a$ under step 3. This describes the inverse natural transformations, including tests meeting multiple coproduct components. The projection to $Z$ is surjective because the base-changed covering is jointly surjective. It is flat and locally of finite presentation: the coproduct components are open immersions, hence etale, and on each component it is a member of that fppf covering; source locality applies to both properties.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), verification of condition (4); descent.tex Tags 04R1,04R3 (lemma-local-source-target-characterize, remark-list-local-source-target).

proof.text: A scheme represents an algebraic space: its functor is an fppf sheaf by representable descent; for scheme tests its diagonal pullbacks are scheme fibre products; the identity is a representable surjective etale atlas. Consequently $A_\beta$ and all the scheme tests in step 4 are algebraic spaces. Apply the fppf atlas bootstrap to the sheaf $F_\beta$ and $q_\beta$: step 4 supplies, for EVERY scheme test and section, a surjective flat locally finitely presented scheme projection. Thus $F_\beta$ is an algebraic space. Choose its representable surjective etale scheme atlas $W_\beta\to F_\beta$. No representability of $F_\beta\to U$ as a scheme has been asserted or needed.

source.place: Tag 04S6 (theorem-final-bootstrap), condition (4); spaces.tex Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space), following lemma-scheme-is-space.

proof.text: Each $L_{\beta\alpha}\to V_\alpha$ is etale: it restricts to the identity on each disjoint open component, and etaleness is local on the source (also for the empty scheme). The atlas base change $W_\beta\times_UV_\alpha\to L_{\beta\alpha}$ is etale by the definition of a representable etale map of sheaves. Its composite to $V_\alpha$ is therefore etale. Since the original fppf covering is fpqc, descent of etaleness for scheme morphisms proves that $W_\beta\to U$ is etale. Here the morphism to which descent applies is the SCHEME morphism $W_\beta\to U$, with base changes $W_\beta\times_UV_\alpha\to V_\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 02VN (lemma-descending-property-etale); Tags 04R1,04R3; morphisms.tex Tag 02GN (lemma-composition-etale); spaces.tex Tag 025Y.

proof.text: The family $\{W_\beta\to U\}_\beta$ is jointly surjective. For $u\in U$, choose $\alpha$ and $v\in V_\alpha$ over $u$. The chosen splitting determines a section of $F_\alpha$ over $V_\alpha$, hence a field-valued point of $F_\alpha$ above $u$. Pulling back its surjective atlas gives a nonempty scheme over that field; any point of this scheme, with its residue field, gives a point of $W_\alpha$ above $u$. Evaluating the atlas map $h_{W_\beta}\to F_\beta$ at the identity yields $P_{M_\beta}|_{W_\beta}\simeq H|_{W_\beta}$ by the definition of $F_\beta$.

source.place: Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space): surjective representable atlas; elementary evaluation and point lifting.

proof.text: Choose an affine open covering $\{U_{\beta t}\to W_\beta\}_t$ for every $\beta$. An open immersion is etale, so its composite $U_{\beta t}\to U$ is etale. These composites are jointly surjective by step 7 and the covering property. Restrict and invert the isomorphism of step 7 to obtain $H\times_U U_{\beta t}\simeq D_{U_{\beta t}}(M_\beta)$; step 1 identifies the right-hand base change. Set $N_{\beta t}=M_\beta$, which is finitely generated by hypothesis. This gives the claimed affine covering. For empty $U$, take the empty family. The zero character group and torsion character groups were included throughout; none of the cited duality, bootstrap or descent statements imposes smoothness, reducedness or a residue-characteristic restriction.

proof_origin.place: Proposition B.3.4, printed pp.290-292 (statement and proof read online); alternative isomorphism-sheaf proof using Appendix B.1 character duality and Stacks 04S6, 02VN. No completion or infinitesimal lifting input.
